It ends with an error when anything is wrong.

project.cli.usage: usage:
redgem                            open the project hub (new / recent games)
redgem <game_dir>                 open the editor
redgem <game_dir> --play          play the game
redgem new <game_dir> [--template {templates}]   create a game
redgem build <game_dir> <out_dir> [--target linux|windows|macos|android] [--bundle]
make a standalone game: an executable (for the Mac, an .app),
an .apk, or with --bundle an App Bundle (.aab) for Google Play
redgem --version                  say which version of RedGem this is
tools that answer in text (each says more with --help):
redgem scene list|get|set|add|remove <game_dir> ...   read and change a scene
redgem run <game_dir> [--seconds N]                   play with no window; say script errors
redgem shot <game_dir> <out.png> [--at seconds]       save a picture of the game at a moment
redgem check <game_dir> [--run-tests]                 look the game over (scripts, scenes, tests)
--gpu auto|dedicated|integrated      graphics card for this run (default: the saved setting,
else the dedicated card when there is one)
redgem <game_dir> --record <out.mp4> [--record-fps 30] [--record-size 3840x2160]
[--record-scale 1920x1080] [--record-seconds N]
play the game into a video (needs ffmpeg): each frame
advances the game by exactly 1/fps, drawn at the size
asked for and scaled to --record-scale; it ends after
N seconds, at Game.stop_recording or when the game quits
Where multiplayer games meet over the internet is a program of its own: redgem-relay;
a game run on a server for players to join is another: redgem-server.
<game_dir> holds {scene_file} (exported from Blender) and a {scripts_dir}/ folder.

project.run.usage: usage: redgem run <game> [--scene name] [--seconds N | --frames N]
plays the game with no window (5 seconds unless said; each frame one fixed step of 1/60 s,
nothing pressed, no sound, saves kept apart from the player's), then says each warning and
error once, with the place in the game's scripts, and a line of summary. It ends with an
error when a script failed. (To play in a window: redgem <game> --play.)

project.scene.script_missing: note: scripts/{script} does not exist yet; it must define class {class}
project.scene.script_not_attached: {script} is not attached; the object has: {scripts}
project.scene.usage: redgem scene list   <game> [--scene name] [--depth N] [--limit N]
<object>  an id (#12, as list shows it), a path (Level/Wall) or a name only one object has
--scene   main (scene.glb, the default) or the name of a file of scenes/
--from    add a copy of that object (and its children); a copy of a prefab is no prefab
keys: position=x,y,z  rotation=x,y,z (degrees)  scale=s or x,y,z  name=N  parent=<object> (parent= : top)
prop.key=value (prop.key= removes it)  script+=Door  script-=Door  script=Door,Sound
project.shot.ended_early: the game ended before that moment: no picture
project.shot.needs_png: the picture's file must end in .png
project.shot.needs_size_and_time: --size needs <width>x<height> (512x288) and --at a number of seconds, 0 or more
project.shot.usage: usage: redgem shot <game> <out.png> [--at seconds] [--scene name] [--size WxH] [--camera name]
plays the game to that moment (1 second unless said), each frame one fixed step, and saves
the picture of that frame, 512x288 unless --size says otherwise. --camera shows the game
through the camera of that object instead of the scene's first camera. It needs a graphics
card (a hidden window is opened to draw with).
